title: Life and property are inviolable
statement: I believe that the life and property of the individual are inviolable. A benevolent society cannot be built on harming people or seizing what they have honestly earned without just cause.
evidence: Without security in person and property, cooperation gives way to fear and predation.
Every durable social contract assumes that innocent people are not legitimate targets of violence or theft.
disproof: Show that a stable, benevolent society can be sustained while routinely violating innocent life or property.

title: Consent is the basis of legitimacy
statement: I believe that consent is the moral basis of legitimate interaction. Unity built on force is domination, not cooperation.
evidence: Voluntary agreements align incentives and reduce resentment.
Coerced participation corrupts both the coerced and the coercer.
disproof: Show that widespread coercion produces more trust, prosperity, and moral integrity than widespread consent.

title: Truth matters more than comfort
statement: I believe that truth matters more than comfort. A benevolent society must prefer painful honesty over soothing falsehood.
evidence: Policies built on pleasant lies eventually harm the people they claim to help.
Trust collapses when leaders and institutions prioritize image over reality.
disproof: Show that societies which suppress uncomfortable truths reliably become more benevolent and unified over time.

title: Law applies equally to all
statement: I believe that law should apply equally to rulers and ruled. Without equal justice, unity becomes obedience to privilege.
evidence: Selective enforcement breeds cynicism and rebellion.
Equal treatment under law is the minimum condition for public trust.
disproof: Show that societies with privileged legal classes remain more peaceful and just than those with equal application of law.

title: Power must be limited and accountable
statement: I believe that power should be limited, divided, and accountable. Concentrated power attracts corruption; benevolence requires checks.
evidence: History shows unchecked power tends toward abuse, even when begun with good intentions.
Separation of powers reduces the cost of any single actor's failure or malice.
disproof: Show that highly concentrated, minimally accountable power consistently produces better outcomes for ordinary people than limited power.

title: Peaceful resolution over violence
statement: I believe that peaceful resolution should be preferred over violence. Force may sometimes be necessary in defense, but it is never a substitute for reason.
evidence: Violence escalates cycles of retaliation and trauma.
Durable agreements require parties to remain alive and willing to coexist.
disproof: Show that societies which routinely choose violence over deliberation become more unified and benevolent.

title: Voluntary exchange benefits both
statement: I believe that voluntary exchange creates mutual benefit. Trade is cooperation, not exploitation, when both parties consent and information is honest.
evidence: People trade when they expect to be better off, not worse off.
Prosperity grows when individuals can specialize and exchange freely.
disproof: Show that banning or heavily restricting voluntary exchange improves welfare more than allowing it under honest rules.

title: Charity is virtuous; coercion is not
statement: I believe that charity is virtuous, but coercion in the name of charity is not. Benevolence must be chosen, or it ceases to be moral.
evidence: Moral credit requires a free choice to help.
Forced 'generosity' often breeds resentment and dependency without dignity.
disproof: Show that coerced redistribution produces stronger character, gratitude, and social trust than voluntary charity.

title: Free speech and honest challenge
statement: I believe that the right to speak, question, and dissent is essential to social health. A society that punishes honest challenge cannot stay truthful or unified for long.
evidence: Error is corrected only when it can be named aloud.
Suppressed speech does not disappear; it festers and returns as extremism.
disproof: Show that suppressing dissent produces more accurate institutions and stronger long-term unity than protecting it.

title: Inherent human worth
statement: I believe that human beings have inherent worth beyond utility. A benevolent society treats people as sacred, not disposable.
evidence: Reducing persons to their economic or political usefulness justifies cruelty.
Dignity is the foundation of both rights and compassion.
disproof: Show that treating human worth as purely instrumental produces a more benevolent and stable society.

title: Persons are not means to ends
statement: I believe that no person should be treated as a means to another's end. Benevolence requires seeing each person as an end in themselves.
evidence: Using people as tools dehumanizes both victim and user.
Kant's categorical imperative remains a practical guardrail against political cruelty.
disproof: Show that routinely instrumentalizing people for collective goals produces better moral outcomes than respecting individual ends.

title: Equal dignity, not equal outcomes
statement: I believe that equal dignity does not require equal outcomes. A benevolent society protects equal standing under the rules, not sameness of result.
evidence: People differ in talent, effort, luck, and choice; equal outcomes require unequal treatment.
Justice concerns fair process; envy concerns comparison.
disproof: Show that enforced equal outcomes increase freedom, trust, and prosperity more than equal rules applied to all.

title: Context matters as much as facts
statement: I believe that context matters as much as facts. Raw facts can mislead when stripped from timing, incentives, or surrounding conditions.
evidence: The same statistic can support opposite conclusions when context is hidden.
Most bad-faith arguments rely on selective framing instead of full reality.
disproof: Show that context regularly makes reasoning less accurate instead of more accurate in high-stakes decisions.

title: Changing your mind is strength
statement: I believe that when better evidence appears, revising a belief is a sign of intellectual integrity, not weakness.
evidence: Stubborn consistency often protects identity rather than truth.
Public reasoning improves when updates are rewarded instead of mocked.
disproof: Show that belief revision predictably harms trust even when the new position is better supported.

title: Principles applied consistently
statement: I believe that principles should be applied consistently, not selectively. Hypocrisy destroys unity because it signals that power, not morality, sets the rules.
evidence: Selective principle application is recognized as injustice even by children.
Double standards dissolve the legitimacy of leaders and institutions.
disproof: Show that societies thrive more when elites routinely exempt themselves from the rules they impose on others.

title: Test morals by consequences
statement: I believe that moral claims should be tested by their real-world consequences. A belief that sounds noble but reliably produces harm should be revised.
evidence: Good intentions are not sufficient when outcomes repeatedly harm the vulnerable.
Evidence over time reveals whether a moral rule actually serves human flourishing.
disproof: Show that moral systems which ignore observed outcomes produce more benevolent societies than those that learn from results.

title: Responsibility alongside rights
statement: I believe that communities thrive when people take responsibility, not only demand rights. Rights without responsibility produce resentment and fracture.
evidence: Sustainable freedom requires citizens who restrain themselves and contribute.
Cultures that emphasize only entitlement tend toward conflict and dependency.
disproof: Show that societies emphasizing rights without personal responsibility become more unified and benevolent.

title: Family and community first
statement: I believe that families and local communities are the first layer of social care. Strong small bonds make large-scale unity possible without tyranny.
evidence: Most care is delivered locally, not by distant bureaucracies.
Healthy families and neighborhoods reduce demand for coercive state intervention.
disproof: Show that weakening family and local community produces stronger benevolence and social trust than strengthening them.

title: Institutions earn trust
statement: I believe that institutions should earn trust through transparency, not demand it through authority. Unity cannot be commanded; it must be justified.
evidence: Opaque institutions breed conspiracy and cynicism.
Transparency allows errors to be corrected before they become catastrophes.
disproof: Show that secretive, unaccountable institutions maintain higher public trust than transparent ones.

title: Property enables planning
statement: I believe that property rights enable long-term planning and investment. People care for what they own and build; societies that undermine ownership undermine prosperity.
evidence: Uncertain property rights discourage saving, building, and maintenance.
Economic development correlates strongly with secure ownership.
disproof: Show that weakening property rights increases investment, care for resources, and long-term prosperity.

title: Opportunity reduces poverty
statement: I believe that poverty is reduced more reliably by opportunity than by resentment. Benevolence should aim at lifting people up, not only redistributing down.
evidence: Markets and mobility have lifted billions out of extreme poverty in recent decades.
Resentment politics often distracts from reforms that expand earning and learning.
disproof: Show that societies focused primarily on resentment and restriction outperform those focused on opportunity and exchange for reducing poverty.

title: Incentives shape behavior
statement: I believe that incentives shape behavior, and good systems align incentives with virtue. A society that rewards cheating will not remain benevolent.
evidence: People respond to what is rewarded and punished, not only to speeches.
Perverse incentives corrupt medicine, education, politics, and business alike.
disproof: Show that incentive structures consistently matter less than rhetoric in determining social outcomes.

title: Honest money and contracts
statement: I believe that honest money and honest contracts are social glue. Deception in economic life destroys trust across the whole society.
evidence: Counterfeiting, fraud, and broken contracts erode cooperation.
Stable exchange requires predictable rules and truthful dealing.
disproof: Show that widespread economic deception strengthens social trust and benevolence.

title: Forgiveness and restoration
statement: I believe that forgiveness and restoration should be possible where truth and repentance exist. Unity requires a path back from failure, not permanent exile for every mistake.
evidence: Societies without mercy become brittle and vengeful.
Restoration preserves families, workplaces, and communities when harm has been acknowledged.
disproof: Show that permanent punishment without restoration produces more benevolent communities than truth-based forgiveness.

title: Gratitude and humility
statement: I believe that gratitude and humility restrain arrogance. Societies that forget gratitude become cruel, even when they call themselves moral.
evidence: Gratitude counters entitlement and tribal hatred.
Humble leaders and citizens are less likely to dehumanize opponents.
disproof: Show that cultures of ingratitude and pride produce more benevolent treatment of the weak than cultures of gratitude and humility.

title: Purpose beyond self-interest
statement: I believe that purpose beyond self-interest gives unity a reason to endure. Shared meaning helps people sacrifice short-term gain for long-term good.
evidence: Pure self-interest alone struggles to sustain sacrifice for strangers or future generations.
Communities with shared purpose weather crises better than those without.
disproof: Show that societies with no transcendent purpose outperform purposeful societies in cooperation and benevolence.

title: Test claims against evidence
statement: I believe that claims about reality should be tested against observable evidence. Benevolence without truth becomes well-intentioned harm.
evidence: Reality does not bend to wishful thinking; policies must answer to results.
Observable outcomes are the final court for factual claims.
disproof: Show a class of important beliefs where objective evidence and observed outcomes should not carry decisive weight.

title: Expertise is not infallible
statement: I believe that expertise is valuable, but expertise is not infallible authority. Science serves society best when it can be questioned openly.
evidence: Expert consensus has been wrong before and will be again.
Progress requires challenge, replication, and revision.
disproof: Show that treating expert authority as beyond question produces better long-term outcomes than open scrutiny.

title: Education teaches how to think
statement: I believe that education should teach people how to think, not only what to think. A unified benevolent society needs citizens who can reason, not just obey narratives.
evidence: Indoctrination produces conformity, not wisdom.
Critical thinking is essential for evaluating leaders, media, and policy.
disproof: Show that education focused on rote acceptance of approved views produces more benevolent citizens than education focused on reasoning.

title: History studied honestly
statement: I believe that history should be studied honestly, including our own failures. Societies that mythologize themselves repeat their worst mistakes.
evidence: Sanitized history prevents learning from past atrocities and errors.
Honest memory is a safeguard against repeating cruelty in new forms.
disproof: Show that nations which suppress uncomfortable history become more just and unified than those that confront it.

title: Prosperity and happiness are life's purpose
statement: I believe the purpose of human life is to prosper and live happily — and that a good society protects the conditions under which each individual can pursue that purpose without initiatory force or coercion.
evidence: People consistently act to improve their own welfare when free to choose.
Societies that protect individual choice and property tend to produce greater prosperity than those built on extraction and control.
disproof: Show that human flourishing is better served when individuals are routinely prevented from pursuing their own prosperity and happiness by initiatory force.

title: My life and happiness come first — morally
statement: I believe I hold supreme the value of my own life and happiness, and that no cause is higher than the life and happiness of the individual. When individual life and property rights are protected, the rights of all people are protected.
evidence: Moral claims that sacrifice identifiable individuals for abstract collective ends have produced mass harm throughout history.
Rights language only coheres when it begins with the inviolable individual, not the group average.
disproof: Show that societies which subordinate individual life and happiness to collective aims reliably produce more prosperity, trust, and moral integrity than those which protect the individual first.

title: No initiatory force, fraud, or coercion
statement: I believe no individual, group, or government may initiate force, threat of force, or fraud against any person or their property — and that force is justified only in defense against those who violate that rule, with no exceptions.
evidence: Initiatory force externalizes cost onto unwilling victims and destroys the basis for voluntary cooperation.
Defensive force answers aggression without licensing perpetual preemption.
disproof: Show that routine initiatory force by governments or majorities produces more freedom, prosperity, and honest dealing than a strict non-aggression principle with defense only.

title: Produce values as a laissez-faire capitalist
statement: I believe I am a laissez-faire capitalist by producing values for others — that real prosperity comes from creating more than I consume, through voluntary exchange, not through political extraction.
evidence: Voluntary production and trade have lifted living standards wherever property and contract are respected.
Value creation aligns self-interest with the welfare of others when exchange is honest and uncoerced.
disproof: Show that societies which penalize production and reward political redistribution outperform market-based value creation on prosperity and individual dignity.

title: The mind identifies reality; it does not create it
statement: I believe the mind does not create objective reality but is an objective-reality-identifying organ — and that integrated thinking requires aligning action with what is real, not with wish or mysticism.
evidence: Actions based on fantasy or evasion fail when reality contradicts them.
Integrated thinking — connecting observations, principles, and consequences — improves decisions over isolated slogans.
disproof: Show that treating the mind as creator rather than discoverer of reality produces better long-term outcomes in science, commerce, and personal life.

title: Teach people to help themselves
statement: I believe the best way to help someone is usually to teach them to help themselves — not to foster permanent dependency that erodes dignity and competence.
evidence: Skills and habits of self-support outlast one-time aid.
Dependency without path to competence breeds resentment on both sides.
disproof: Show that long-term one-way assistance without teaching self-reliance produces more competent, grateful, and prosperous people than empowerment toward independence.

title: Replace the truth oath with contextual honesty
statement: I believe the legal system should replace the truth oath with a contextual honesty oath — because raw factual statements stripped of context can mislead as effectively as lies.
evidence: Selective truth-telling is a common tool of deception in law, politics, and commerce.
Contextual honesty requires full relevant disclosure, not technically true fragments.
disproof: Show that the traditional truth oath produces more accurate justice and less manipulation in court than an oath requiring contextual honesty.

title: Morality tracks benefit and harm to the human organism
statement: I believe all things good for the human organism and its biological needs are morally correct, all things bad for the organism are morally incorrect, and anything else is not a moral issue.
evidence: Moral confusion often comes from treating taste, tradition, or taboo as moral law.
Grounding morality in life and harm clarifies what is actually at stake in ethical disputes.
disproof: Show a coherent moral framework that ignores organismic benefit and harm yet produces clearer, more benevolent guidance for how people should treat one another.

title: Rational choice links reality, prosperity, and love
statement: I believe rational, free choice is the prerequisite for integrating reality with human nature — which is the prerequisite for prosperity and happiness, and in turn for romantic love.
evidence: Coerced 'choices' do not integrate values with reality because the chooser is not free to reject error.
Deep relationships require persons who can think, choose, and take responsibility for their lives.
disproof: Show that removing rational free choice from major life domains improves individual prosperity, happiness, and capacity for genuine romantic partnership.

title: I am responsible for my prosperity and happiness
statement: I believe I am responsible for my prosperity, happiness, success, and romantic love — not as a denial of hardship, but as the stance required to use my mind, act on reality, and refuse victimhood as an identity.
evidence: Agency is the precondition for improvement; abdication of responsibility forecloses learning.
External barriers exist, but permanent surrender of responsibility guarantees permanent stagnation.
disproof: Show that individuals who treat themselves as powerless victims of circumstance reliably achieve more prosperity and happiness than those who take responsibility within their sphere of action.

title: Law stops injustice; it does not create justice
statement: I believe law exists to stop injustice — not to create justice by force. When law tries to manufacture outcomes, it often produces new injustice in the name of good intentions.
evidence: Justice as an outcome emerges from voluntary exchange, restitution, and consistent rules — not from decree alone.
Legislated 'social justice' schemes frequently violate innocents while failing to deliver promised equity.
disproof: Show that laws designed to create positive justice by force consistently outperform limited laws that only prohibit injustice.

title: Produce more value than you consume
statement: I believe I should produce more values than I consume — that net production is both a moral commitment and the practical basis of prosperity for myself and others.
evidence: Chronic consumption without production depletes what others have built.
Wealth and welfare grow when individuals specialize, produce, and trade surplus.
disproof: Show that societies thrive more when most members consume persistently more than they produce than when net production is the norm.
